card.title: Admit You’re Hurt
card.instruction: Get someone to admit hurt, fear, or disappointment before you reveal that you feel it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did the boss calling us office furniture hurt you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? Are you making a complaint?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's still in drafts. How did you feel?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Invisible. I've worked here twelve years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Me too. Mine says 'unprofessional'; I'm changing that to 'I went home and cried.'

mechanism: A probes B's hurt at a workplace insult before revealing the emotional content behind A's draft complaint.
confusable: Unlike gathering witnesses only, A must disclose shared feeling after the other person names theirs.
comparison: D112-b shifts complaint language after B's invisibility admission; D112-a discloses matching tears after B goes first.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
